selected.text: these days which are in truth the source of all days, and in this age which is the king of ages, the friends of the All-Merciful should strive with the utmost joy and fragrance to attain lofty stations and enduring ranks, for the world is seen to be as a shadow that exists one moment and is gone the next. The upright souls who have turned to God should hold fast to the cord of His grace and exert their utmost effort that perchance some service may be rendered by them for God's sake, the effects of which will remain and endure in the world. If one would awaken even slightly and reflect upon the changes in the world, everything that exists therein, even while appearing to exist, testifies to its own transience and extinction. Blessed are they of insight who today have not been deprived by any veil from the Most Great Vision and who day and night are occupied with uniting hearts and bringing souls together
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s reflection that the world is a passing shadow and that blessed are they who day and night are occupied with uniting hearts; sets fellowship against transience.

selected.text: Unity of the heart between the friends of God attracts the outpouring of the Holy Spirit and capable souls receive the bounty of the divine Mysteries and they become the distributors of the Light... … Inharmony destroys the magnet to attract the Divine Elixir and all become deprived. This is a great loss; therefore, one must study to promote this Unity, which is essential to the life of the believers
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that unity of heart attracts the Holy Spirit while inharmony destroys the magnet; develops the magnet image.

selected.text: The people of Baha must be the cause of uniting all the nations.  They must dispel inharmony and dispute. So now we must consider deeply how the Baha'is must really be, what characteristics they must have and what actions they must perform. … And if there is not this love and harmony among Baha'is how can they cause it to appear among the inhabitants of the earth? How can an ill man nurse others? How could a pauper give wealth to others? So the first thing the Baha'is must do is to feel love and unity in their hearts before they can spread it among others
selected.reason: Reported message of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how an ill man can nurse others, so that Bahá’ís must first feel love among themselves before spreading it; the guide’s link between community and humanity.

selected.text: They must remain firm and steadfast in the Cause of the Lord of the Day of Judgment with perfect unity and accord. … O friends of Truth! The people are without fairness and are worshippers of idle fancies. For years they have worshipped and bowed down before the idols of vain imaginings. I beseech the True One, the Mighty, the Powerful, to protect His party and grant them the heavenly water of reality, that all may become intoxicated with the wine of knowledge and occupied with the remembrance of the Peerless Friend
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to steadfast unity beside His description of a people worshipping the idols of vain imaginings; strong polemical language kept with its source.

selected.text: Differences between the friends in any matter whatsoever causes weakness in the Cause of God and leads to the wavering of souls … Consider that when differences arise, inevitably one party is supported while the other party becomes broken-hearted and sorrowful, and ulterior motives emerge and become a cause of veiling … You must have utmost fellowship with each other and strive that if any difference arises, even between two people, to quickly remove it so that its scope does not expand
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s analysis of how differences leave one party broken-hearted and breed ulterior motives, with the charge to remove any difference quickly before it spreads.

selected.text: Be among the concourse of all created things with spirit and fragrance, that they may inhale from you the sweet savors of the Beloved. This, verily, is true victory, were you of those who know. Beware lest there appear from you that which would cause division in the Cause.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to move among all things with such fragrance that they inhale the savors of the Beloved, calling this true victory; redefines victory as conduct.

selected.text: O loved ones of God in His lands! Hearken unto the call of the Wronged One which hath been raised from the precincts of the Prison. There is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Great. Be ye united in the Cause of God and His remembrance, and be ye as the fingers of one hand.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call from the Prison to be united in the Cause and His remembrance as the fingers of one hand; a compact image of unity under persecution.

selected.text: The letter adorned with the ink of love, which is in truth the cause and reason for, and manifestation of, the unity of the servants in the Cause of the Lord of creation, became the source of joy and gladness and the cause of delight and felicity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s description of a letter written in the ink of love as the cause and manifestation of the unity of the servants; letters as bonds.

selected.text: O people of God! Ye must needs be so steadfast in the Cause of God that neither the onslaught of the mighty nor their ascendancy may weaken you. Stand ye for God's sake and speak for God's sake.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to such steadfastness that the onslaught of the mighty cannot weaken the believers; steadfastness under persecution.

selected.text: Then I counsel you that ye dispute not in the Cause of God, even should the idolaters unite against you, and be ye in the earth as standards of victory from One wise and self-subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel not to dispute in the Cause of God even should opponents unite, but to stand as standards of victory; restraint under pressure.

selected.text: The purpose of these people is to create division in the Cause of God and destroy the unity of the Baha'is, so that in the process they may pursue their selfish desires.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s warning that certain people seek to divide the Cause and destroy Bahá’í unity for selfish desires; polemical language retained with its attribution.

selected.text: Beware lest ye differ in the Cause - gather ye on the shore of this Most Great Sea. By My life! Through your unity the pillars of the deniers shall be demolished.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to gather on the shore of the Most Great Sea, for through unity the pillars of the deniers shall be demolished; the guide’s representative call to spiritual victory.

selected.text: O people, fear ye God and differ not among yourselves, lest the hearts of the deniers rejoice thereat. Be as one soul in upholding the Cause
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s command not to differ lest the hearts of the deniers rejoice, but to be as one soul in upholding the Cause.

selected.text: the branches of Iraq, and this was ordained by the All-Wise, the All-Knowing. Dispute not after Me, but gather ye together around the Cause, for this is what God desired for you in the atomic realm before the creation of the heavens

selected.text: O loved ones of God in the cities and regions! Know ye that power lieth in unity, and prosperity and success in steadfastness and concord.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that power lies in unity and prosperity and success in steadfastness and concord.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning to avoid discord, since through it the pure cup of mystical knowledge is sullied; the spiritual cost of division in His own words.

selected.text: The purpose hath ever been and will ever be the unity of the loved ones, for if this matter is not achieved, nothing is achieved.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the purpose has ever been the unity of the loved ones, for if it is not achieved nothing is achieved; a foundational claim.

selected.text: Rather, resolve the differences that have arisen between you and be as brothers firmly established upon the thrones of unity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to resolve the differences that have arisen and be as brothers established upon the thrones of unity; His direct call to repair.

selected.text: Be ye united in the Cause of God and differ not as did the people before you. Fear ye God, O people of understanding!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s command to be united and not differ as did the peoples before; places unity in the history of religion.

selected.text: That which is essential today in that land is the unity of the friends of God, as well as the observance of wisdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that what is essential in that land is the unity of the friends and the observance of wisdom; pairs unity with prudence.

selected.text: True unity is to fix one's gaze upon the horizon of the One Manifestation and to be detached and free from all else
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s definition of true unity as fixing one’s gaze on the One Manifestation and being detached from all else; a theological definition.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the loved ones united as one hand, standing on one foot and soaring on one wing; a vivid picture of concerted life.

selected.text: is that you should convey greetings on behalf of this ephemeral one to the loved ones of God--those souls who have drunk from the ocean of love and are gazing toward and turned to the horizon of grace--and make mention that today is the day of the remembrance of God, and today is the day of service and assistance. Time must not be lost, and the purpose of service and assistance is the mention of Truth through wisdom and utterance, that perchance the scattered letters of the world may be gathered together in the temple of a single word, and that word may become the cause of the completion and adornment of the Book of Creation
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s hope that service through wisdom and utterance gather the scattered letters of the world into the temple of a single word; a striking image of gathered humanity.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O God, O my God, at this moment, by Him Whom Thou hast made a treasure for all created things, a shelter for all existence, and a fortress for all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, to send down upon our hearts the love of Thy loved ones and the affection of Thy chosen ones, that we may become pure mirrors, holy crystals, and luminous lamps, reflecting the wonders of the pure camphor of Thy countenance and proclaiming the gleamings of the cloud of might of Thy presence, that we may be as one servant and one soul in the earth, all prostrating before the sovereign of Thy majesty and submitting to the king of Thy beauty, for we are all Thy servants and within Thy grasp.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer for the love of His loved ones, that all may become pure mirrors and luminous lamps as one servant and one soul.

selected.text: The first watering of this real plantation is unity among the friends of God. To-day there is nothing so essential and so indispensable for the glory and honor of the Bahai cause as the unity of the beloved of God. The more the friends of God are united the greater will be the success attending their efforts … Therefore I beg and counsel you to continue in good fellowship and unity, to co-operate with and be kind toward one another, to exalt one another, and to be the means of comfort and ease to one another, in order that other nations may learn from you how great are the fruits of unity
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Oakland calling unity the first watering of the plantation and asking the friends to exalt and comfort one another so nations may learn its fruits.

selected.text: But the fault-finders constantly seek to scatter and disperse the divine sheep and desire the disarray of the party of the All-Merciful, for as long as the sheep are gathered and preserved, protected and blessed under the shadow of the True Shepherd, there is no benefit for any fault-finder and no advantage for any attacker.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of fault-finders seeking to scatter the sheep who are safe while gathered under the True Shepherd; the threat of division in pastoral terms.

selected.text: Whenever ye find someone desiring to separate himself from the flock, it is incumbent upon you to treat him with fragrance and kindness and persuade and encourage him, so that this secluded sheep may return to the flock.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s instruction to treat anyone wishing to separate from the flock with kindness and encouragement so that he may return; care for the one drifting away.

selected.text: Therefore the desire of the Ancient Beauty for His loved ones is that they should stand firm upon a single path, for the discord among the loved ones of God brings joy to the enemies and sorrow to His chosen ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that discord among the loved ones brings joy to the enemies and sorrow to His chosen ones; why division is costly.

selected.text: Ye must strive with the utmost endeavor to unite souls and bring hearts together. In every place where discord hath arisen between the friends, it hath caused the Cause to be wasted and extinguished the fire of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that wherever discord has arisen between the friends it has wasted the Cause and extinguished the fire of God; the gravity of division.

selected.text: Today, the greatest of all things are love, fellowship, unity, harmony, detachment, freedom, sanctification, purity, sacrifice, and the joy of God's loved ones. If perfect fellowship and pure love are not achieved, all these efforts and hardships will be wasted, and all will ultimately suffer evident loss. The purpose of the manifestation of Truth and the rising of the Sun of Reality is the triumph of the light of God's love, so that the darkness of discord and dissension may vanish from the horizons and spiritual unity may appear. All the friends are as one soul, and all names and attributes are expressions of one person.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that without perfect fellowship and pure love every effort and hardship is wasted, since the purpose of Revelation is spiritual unity; sets the stakes of the subject.

selected.text: We who are servants at the same Threshold are bound together by bonds of cordial fellowship at all times so that the perfume of one heart can make the other fragrant. We are connected through our mutual attraction to the divine kingdom in such wise that we can expound spiritual mysteries even like the wires of the telegraph!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of hearts so bound that the perfume of one makes another fragrant, connected like the wires of the telegraph; a distinctive account of spiritual communion.

selected.text: Consider this passage from the Gospel when Christ's brothers came to Him and said "These are Your brothers." He replied that His brothers were those who believed in God, and He refused to associate and commune with His brothers. … Similarly, Qurratu'l-Ayn, who was renowned throughout all regions, when she believed in God and was attracted to the divine fragrances, detached herself from her two elder sons because they did not believe, and never met with them again, although they were her two capable sons. She would say that all the beloved of God were her sons, but these two were not her sons at all and she was detached from them
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account of Christ and of Qurratu’l-Ayn placing spiritual kinship above physical kinship; a demanding passage the guide reads with its historical circumstances.

selected.text: Be ye to each other as heavenly lovers and divine beloved ones. Spend your life in the paradise of love. Build your nest on the leafy branches of the tree of love. Soar ye in the clear atmosphere of love. Swim ye in the shoreless sea of love. Walk ye in the eternal rose-garden of love. Move ye in the shining rays of the sun of love. Be ye firm and steadfast in the path of love. Perfume your nostrils with the sweet fragrance of the flowers of love. Familiarize your ears with the soul-entrancing melodies of love. Be ye intoxicated with the wine of love. Drink we deeply of the elixir of love. Let your ideals be the bouquet of love, and your conversation the white pearls of the ocean of love.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in a sustained litany asking the friends to nest, soar, swim and walk in love; the guide’s most lyrical portrait of fellowship.

selected.text: When the Beauty of the All-Merciful shed His luminous rays upon the world of being, that light of reality shone forth in pure hearts. True fellowship, heartfelt love, and eternal brotherhood became manifest and evident, for all were illumined by one light, drew sustenance from one Revelation, and were brightened by the flame of Sinai. This brotherhood is of the Kingdom, divine, heavenly, spiritual, eternal, everlasting.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account of true fellowship and eternal brotherhood appearing when all were illumined by one Revelation; traces fellowship to its spiritual source.

selected.text: Moreover, I beseech you that in these few remaining days of your life, ye live with one another in utmost kindness and mercy, but resting and reposing in the shade of His special favor, for that is the foundation throughout all cycles and the aim in every age. Hold fast to the glory of His loving-kindness and cling to the cord of His forgiveness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s plea that in the few remaining days of life the friends live with one another in utmost kindness and mercy; a tender counsel on the brevity of life.

selected.text: if a number of the Baha'is go there with the spirit of unity, and calling the people by day and by night to the Kingdom of Abha and giving the Glad-tidings to all the religions and sects and live together with the utmost of good fellowship and show toward each other love and unity, that it may set others to think and wonder - it is very praiseworthy
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s praise for Bahá’ís who settle in a place and live together in such fellowship that others are moved to think and wonder; community life as witness.

selected.text: I ask God that thou mayest, in that region, make the friends to be companions and associates to one another and enable all to be gathered together and strengthened through unity, harmony and love. Thus may they, through companionship and fellowship, become enthralled and enkindled, be filled with joy and exultation, and increase in love and attachment.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer that a believer may make the friends of a region companions to one another, strengthened by unity and love.

selected.text: The fellowship of friends brings about spirit and fragrance, and the love of brethren induces joy in heart and soul, especially spiritual brethren and mystical friends. As much as thou canst, associate with souls from whose heart-gardens thou canst inhale the sweet fragrance of the love of God, and from whose luminous foreheads thou canst behold the manifest light.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to associate with souls from whose heart-gardens the fragrance of the love of God can be inhaled; a last word on companionship.

selected.text: Therefore, Ye should love the friends with all your hearts and souls and offer up your lives for one another. Deny them not any service. Do not consider any hardship to be too difficult. Let each one become the beloved of one and all, and the object of one another's attention. This is the requirement of love and the foundation of amity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to deny the friends no service, count no hardship too difficult and let each become the beloved of all; names this the foundation of amity.

selected.text: Likewise when people of faith associate with material minded people their hearts are depressed too. Therefore whenever you meet the friends of God be very happy; speak about spiritual things so that you may find heavenly susceptibilities. Association of the friends is the greatest of divine bounties.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that association with the material-minded depresses the heart while the association of the friends is the greatest of divine bounties.

selected.text: In this corporeal world, despite the separation of bodies, friends remain friends and intimate with each other. In the eternal world, then, which is the world of divine unity and heavenly oneness, friendship and spiritual intimacy are naturally among the essential requisites of that sanctified world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that friends remain intimate despite bodily separation and that friendship is essential in the eternal world; the guide’s account of friendship after death.

selected.text: Among the friends, fellowship and unity become the cause of familiarizing strangers and spread to all, for the divine friends are as the heart of humanity. Whatever shines forth and surges in the heart permeates all members, such that the eye weeps, the lip smiles, and the entire being begins to dance and move.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of the friends as the heart of humanity, whose fellowship spreads to all members as feeling spreads through a body; how inner unity reaches others.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on one who found solace in the company of the loved ones amid His sufferings; companionship under persecution.

selected.text: Fellowship makes every difficulty easy for man. These farmers now, despite such hardships, despite such an arduous life, find it a paradise because of their fellowship. … Man must cultivate fellowship, must establish intimate association

selected.reason: Reported advice of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to schoolboys in ‘Akká not to be corrupted by the evil-minded and to counsel one another on living noble lives; companionship in moral education.

selected.text: Whoso desireth to sit with God, let him sit with My loved ones - this is a revelation from One Who is Mighty, All-Knowing. And whoso desireth to inhale the fragrance of the garment, let him inhale it from My chosen ones
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that whoever desires to sit with God should sit with His loved ones; gives companionship its spiritual meaning.

selected.text: God willing, thou shouldst in all conditions fix thy gaze upon the All-Glorious and associate and consort with upright souls, illumined hearts and steadfast minds. Thus doth the Beloved counsel thee out of love for thyself.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s loving counsel to consort with upright souls, illumined hearts and steadfast minds; the positive form of choosing companions.

selected.text: The divine friends are waves of one sea and drops of one river, flowers of one garden and fragrances of one rose garden, stars of one heaven and lamps of one chamber. They must care for one another and be kind to each other.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s images of the friends as waves of one sea, flowers of one garden and lamps of one chamber who must care for one another; introduces the sea and garden images the questions compare.

selected.text: At one time We name friendship an ornament for the temple of man, and at another time a crown for his head and a light for his countenance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s naming of friendship as an ornament for the temple of man, a crown for his head and a light for his countenance; a memorable praise of friendship.

selected.text: The friends must be like this, becoming the lowliest servants to one another, adopting the principle of the oneness of mankind, and walking in the ways of the denizens of the highest paradise.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel that the friends become the lowliest servants to one another while adopting the oneness of mankind; ties humble service to the universal principle.

selected.text: A friend is one who remains a friend's friend in times of distress and helplessness. Truly he has shown the utmost faithfulness. Know his worth.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s definition of a friend as one who remains a friend in times of distress and helplessness; answers the guide’s opening question about what makes a friend.

selected.text: Friendship is a sun created by God for the heaven of humanity - through it his station is exalted and his worth becomes manifest among the peoples
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of friendship as a sun created by God for the heaven of humanity, through which a person’s worth is made manifest; gives friendship its highest dignity.

selected.text: The poet spoke truly when he said that three things are scarce, namely, the demon, the phoenix and the faithful friend. Yes, like the demon and the phoenix, the true friend is rare. But under the shadow of the Word of God, the Blessed Beauty has produced such friends for you.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá citing a poet that the faithful friend is as rare as the phoenix, yet such friends have been raised up; returns to what makes a friend.

selected.text: Brotherhood is of two kinds: physical and spiritual. Physical brotherhood has no significance since it derives from the element of water and clay, not from heart and soul. But spiritual brotherhood is firm and strong since it derives from the essence of the honored spirit and is supremely precious and respected.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s distinction between physical brotherhood of water and clay and spiritual brotherhood of the spirit; the guide’s key statement on spiritual kinship.

selected.text: Become so intimate with each other that you are viewed as one person and considered as the manifestation of heavenly unity, for the heavenly relationship is so strong that it cannot be dissolved for all eternity. … In this world it is a perfect happiness and in the realm of Heaven it will continue to shine in eternal splendor
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to become so intimate as to be viewed as one person, since the heavenly relationship cannot be dissolved for all eternity; anticipates the guide’s close.

selected.text: In any case, though outwardly we are distant and separated, and in burning anguish from the fire of separation, yet as we are intoxicated from the same wine and delighted and joyous from the favors of the Forgiving Lord, we are immersed in one sea and wandering in one desert, birds of one rose garden and fish of one ocean. Therefore we are intimate companions
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s assurance that though outwardly separated, friends are fish of one ocean and birds of one rose garden; friendship through absence.

selected.text: The purpose is that I have the utmost love for you, and I hope through the favors of the Most Great Name that day by day these bonds will become stronger and the divine friends will show love to one another and become so enkindled with the fire of the love of God that they become the pulsating force in the veins and arteries of the world, and become outpouring clouds upon the plains and deserts of the heart and soul of the world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s hope that the friends become the pulsating force in the veins and arteries of the world and outpouring clouds on its deserts.

selected.text: What manner of attachment and connection is this, and what manner of love and fellowship, that like an impregnable fortress of steel stands firm and established
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s wonder at a love and fellowship that stands like an impregnable fortress of steel; the strength of the bond between particular friends.

selected.text: association with these loved ones is, before God, more beloved than all else. I swear by God that to gaze upon these faces is greater and more acceptable than seventy years of worship
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that to gaze upon the faces of His loved ones is more acceptable than seventy years of worship; the worth of fellowship before God.

selected.text: Go to see each other and be consoling friends to all. If a friend lives a little distance from the town, go to see him.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to visit and console one another, even a friend living a little distance from the town; the guide’s simplest practical act of care.

selected.text: Whatever there is, we are together - companions, sharing the same condition, working together, and walking the same path.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that whatever there is, we are together, companions sharing the same condition and walking the same path; the essence of companionship.

To inflict persecution upon One is to persecute the Others. In all degrees of existence each One praises and sanctifies the Others. Each of Them holds to the solidarity of mankind and promotes the unity of human hearts. Next to the divine Manifestations come the believers whose characteristics are agreement, fellowship and love. The Baha'i friends in Persia attained such a brotherhood and love that it really became a hindrance in the conduct of material affairs. Each one into whatever house of the friends he went considered himself the owner of the house, so to speak. There was no duality but complete mutuality of interests and love. The visiting friend would have no hesitation in opening the provision box and taking out enough food for his needs. They wore each other's clothes as their own when necessary. If in need of a hat or cloak, they would take and use it. The owner of the clothing would be thankful and grateful that the garment had gone. When he returned home, he would perhaps be told, "So and so was here and took away your coat." He would reply, "Praise be to God! I am so grateful to him. Praise be to God! I am so thankful I have been given this opportunity of showing my love for him." To such an extreme degree this love and fellowship expressed itself that Baha'u'llah commanded that no one should take possession of another's belongings unless presented with them. The intention is to show to what an extent unity and love prevailed among the Baha'i friends in the East.

selected.text: There are persons with whom you associate and converse whose utterances are life-imparting, joy-giving.
